newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU offers aid to flood-damaged eastern Germany.
newsitem.headline: EU offers aid to flood-damaged eastern Germany.

text.p: The European Union proposed on Wednesday 1.5 billion Ecu in relief aid for the German state of Brandenburg in order to help the battered region cope with the worst flooding seen in more than 200 years.

EU Regional Affairs Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies told a news conference that the European Commission would consult the European Parliament over the proposed aid. It was unclear how quickly the money would be made available.
"This is an absolute necessary decision," Wulf-Mathies told reporters, adding that she would visit the region on Friday.
Floods along the River Oder on the German-Polish border showed signs of receding on Wednesday after a fresh high-water surge expected overnight did not materialise, officials in eastern Germany said.
There has been no loss of life in eastern Germany, but damage to homes, farms and businesses has been extensive.
A significant portion of the aid would be used to repair sewage and waste disposal systems and ensuring safe drinking water.
